323975.title: The monomial-count conjecture for eigenvectors of Markov matrices
323975.statement: Let $A$ be the $n\times n$ matrix given by equation (44), and let $\mathbf{v}$ be the eigenvector given by equation (29). Express each coordinate of $\mathbf{v}$ in terms of the variables $\tau_{ij}$. **Monomial-count conjecture.** Each coordinate is the sum of $n^{n-2}$ monomials, each with coefficient $1$. The claim is motivated by the observed counts $1,3,16,125,1296$ for $n=2,3,4,5,6$, respectively; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

324517.title: Characterization of assembly graphs with genus range {0,1}
324517.statement:
Let a **double occurrence word (DOW)** be a word in which every letter occurs exactly twice, and let $[?]$ denote the graph corresponding to a DOW under the construction used in the paper. For a graph $[?]$, write ${\rm gr}([?])$ for its genus range. A word is **loop-nested** when it is obtained by loop nesting from another word.

**Genus-range characterization.** Any DOW whose corresponding graph has genus range $\{0,1\}$ is obtained from the word

$$
w=12\cdots n12\cdots n
$$

for an odd integer $n$ by loop nesting.

This would characterize all DOWs giving genus range $\{0,1\}$, extending the preceding results on loop-nested words and repeat words. The source provides no resolution status for this conjecture.

324645.title: Lewis's even-length alternating-pattern enumeration conjecture
324645.statement:
Let $A_n(\sigma)$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$ that avoid the pattern $\sigma$ and are alternating. **Lewis's conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$ and $\sigma \in \{1243,2134,1432,3214,2341,4123,3421,4312\}$, we have

$$
|A_{2n}(\sigma)|=|A_{2n}(1234)|=|A_{2n}(2143)|.
$$

These equalities concern the enumeration of even-length alternating permutations avoiding patterns of length four; the common value for the two reference patterns is the $3$-dimensional Catalan number $\frac{2(3n)!}{n!(n+1)!(n+2)!}$. The statement was posed by Lewis and its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.

324646.title: Lewis's odd-length alternating-pattern enumeration conjecture for 2134, 4312, 3214 and 4123
324646.statement:
Let $A_n(\sigma)$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$ that avoid the pattern $\sigma$ and are alternating. **Lewis's conjecture.** For $n\geq 0$ and $\sigma \in \{2134,4312,3214,4123\}$, we have

$$
|A_{2n+1}(\sigma)|=|A_{2n+1}(1234)|.
$$

This predicts equal enumerations for odd-length alternating permutations avoiding each of the four specified patterns and avoiding $1234$. The statement was posed by Lewis, and the supplied text does not specify whether it has been resolved.

329992.title: A shifted-coset formula for rational Catalan polynomials
329992.statement:
Let $a<b$ be relatively prime. Let $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}$ be the lattice of $a$-cores, let $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_T=(a\mathbb{Z})^{a-1}$, and let $\mathfrak{c}$ range over the cosets in $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}/\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_T$. For each coset, let $s(\mathfrak{c},b)$ denote the shift determining the intersection of the coset with the simplex of $(a,b)$-cores, and let $\mathcal{SC}_{a-1}(b)$ denote that simplex.

**Coset age conjecture.** There is an age function $\iota$ on the cosets $\mathfrak{c}\in\boldsymbol{\Lambda}/\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_T$ such that

$$
\sum_{\mathfrak{c}\in\boldsymbol{\Lambda}/\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_T}q^{\iota(\mathfrak{c})}=[a]_{q^2}[a]_{q^3}\cdots[a]_{q^{a-1}}
$$

and

$$
\mathbf{Cat}_{a,b}(q)=\sum_{\mathfrak{c}\in\boldsymbol{\Lambda}/\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_T}q^{\iota(\mathfrak{c})}\binom{b/a-s(\mathfrak{c},b)+a-1}{a-1}_{q^a},
$$

where the $q^a$-binomial coefficient $q^a$-counts the points in $\mathfrak{c}\cap\mathcal{SC}_{a-1}(b)$. This would provide a shifted lattice-point expression for the rational Catalan polynomial and explain the positivity of its coefficients. The source presents this as conjectural and gives no resolution.

330233.title: Support rigidity conjecture for Liouville currents of flat metrics
330233.statement:
Let $S$ be the underlying surface and let $\mathrm{Flat}(S)$ denote the space of flat metrics on $S$. For $\varphi\in\mathrm{Flat}(S)$, let $L_{\varphi}$ be its Liouville geodesic current and let $\mathrm{supp}(L_{\varphi})$ denote its support. Scaling a metric by $a>0$ preserves this support, and affine deformations arising from $SL_2(\mathbb R)$ actions on metrics defined by holomorphic quadratic differentials also preserve it. **Support rigidity conjecture.** Given $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in\mathrm{Flat}(S)$, if

$$
\mathrm{supp}(L_{\varphi_1})=\mathrm{supp}(L_{\varphi_2}),
$$

then there exists an affine map $f\colon(S,\varphi_1)\to(S,\varphi_2)$ isotopic to the identity. Equivalently, up to this affine ambiguity, the support of the Liouville current determines the flat metric. The paper proves that the full marked length spectrum determines a flat metric, and studies how much information is already contained in the support of its Liouville current. The conjecture asserts that the scaling and affine deformations described in the open questions are the only possible ambiguities.

332680.title: Modified Orlik's conjecture for characteristic-polynomial divisibility
332680.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{A}}$ be an $\ell$-arrangement and let $H\in{\mathcal{A}}$. Write ${\mathcal{A}}'={\mathcal{A}}\setminus\{H\}$, and let $\pi({\mathcal{A}};t)$ denote the Poincaré polynomial. Assume that ${\mathcal{A}}$ is free and that

$$
\pi({\mathcal{A}}^H;t)\text{ divides }\pi({\mathcal{A}};t).
$$

Equivalently, assume that $\pi({\mathcal{A}}';t)$ divides $\pi({\mathcal{A}};t)$. **Modified Orlik's conjecture.** There exists an arrangement ${\mathcal{A}}$ and $H\in{\mathcal{A}}$ such that, for the triple $({\mathcal{A}},{\mathcal{A}}',{\mathcal{A}}^H)$, (1) $\pi({\mathcal{A}}^H;t)=\prod_{i=1}^{\ell-1}(1+d_it)$ with $d_1,\ldots,d_{\ell-1}\in\mathbb{Z}$; (2) $\pi({\mathcal{A}}^H;t)$ divides both $\pi({\mathcal{A}};t)$ and $\pi({\mathcal{A}}';t)$; and (3) neither ${\mathcal{A}}$ nor ${\mathcal{A}}'$ is free, or ${\mathcal{A}}$ is free and ${\mathcal{A}}'$ is not free.

The source introduces this as a conjectural counterexample to the stronger modified Orlik problem. The stated belief is that the problem is too strong and that such an arrangement exists; no resolution is supplied in the provided text.

336583.title: Sufficiency of the correspondence-graph connectivity condition for rigidity
336583.statement: Let a configuration consist of sensor and anchor points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, with correspondence graph $\Gamma$. Assume the paper's standing Assumption, and suppose that any $k\geq d+1$ points in $\mathcal{X}_s\cup\mathcal{X}_a$ are non-degenerate. The graph $\Gamma$ is **quasi $k$-connected** if any two vertices in its correspondence-vertex class have at least $k$ paths that are vertex-disjoint over its point-vertex class, and some pair has exactly $k$ such paths. **The rigidity conjecture.** Under these assumptions, the configuration is rigid in $\mathbb{R}^d$ if and only if its correspondence graph is quasi $(d+1)$-connected. The paper proves quasi $(d+1)$-connectivity as a necessary condition for rigidity; the conjecture asserts sufficiency as well, based on empirical evidence, and no counterexample is known in the source.

340009.title: The inversion-major-index equidistribution conjecture for reduced words of the longest permutation
340009.statement:
Let $w_0^{(n)}$ be the longest permutation in $athcalS_n$ and let $\operatorname{Red}(w_0^{(n)})$ denote its reduced words. For a reduced word $\rho$, define its inversion statistic $\operatorname{inv}(\rho)$ as in the paper, and define the major index by

$$
\operatorname{maj}(\rho)=\sum_{i:\,\rho_{i+1}>\rho_i}i.
$$

**Inversion-major-index equidistribution conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$,

$$
\sum_{\rho\in\operatorname{Red}(w_0^{(n)})}q^{\operatorname{inv}(\rho)}=\frac{\left[\binom{n}{2}\right]_q!}{[1]_q^{n-1}[3]_q^{n-2}[5]_q^{n-3}\cdots[2n-3]_q^1}=\sum_{\rho\in\operatorname{Red}(w_0^{(n)})}q^{\operatorname{maj}(\rho)-\binom{n}{3}}.
$$

The displayed identity is a proposed $q$-analogue of the known major-index formula for reduced words of the longest permutation, relating the newly defined inversion statistic to the major index. The supplied text does not state whether this conjecture has been proved or disproved.

340444.title: Kanade–Russell product identities
340444.statement:
Let $q$ be a formal variable, and for $1\leq \ell\leq 11$ let $H_\ell(x;q)$ be the series defined above from the sums over $i,j,k\geq 0$ and the specified polynomials $A_\ell(i,j,k)$. Write $(a_1,\ldots,a_r;q)_\infty=\prod_{m\geq0}\prod_{s=1}^r(1-a_sq^m)$. **Kanade–Russell conjecture.** The series are equal to the following products:

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_1(1)&=\frac{1}{(q,q^4,q^6,q^8,q^{11};q^{12})_\infty},&H_2(1)&=\frac{(q^6;q^{12})_\infty}{(q^2,q^3,q^4;q^6)_\infty},\\
H_3(1)&=\frac{1}{(q^4,q^5,q^6,q^7,q^8;q^{12})_\infty},&H_4(1)&=\frac{1}{(q;q^4)_\infty(q^4,q^{11};q^{12})_\infty},\\
H_5(1)&=\frac{1}{(q;q^4)_\infty(q^7,q^8;q^{12})_\infty},&H_6(1)&=\frac{(q^3;q^{12})_\infty}{(q,q^2;q^4)_\infty},\\
H_7(1)&=\frac{(q^9;q^{12})_\infty}{(q^2,q^3;q^4)_\infty},&H_8(1)&=\frac{1}{(q^3;q^4)_\infty(q,q^8;q^{12})_\infty},\\
H_9(1)&=\frac{1}{(q^3;q^4)_\infty(q^4,q^5;q^{12})_\infty},&H_{10}(1)&=\frac{1}{(q;q^3)_\infty(q^3,q^6,q^{11};q^{12})_\infty},\\
H_{11}(1)&=\frac{1}{(q^2;q^3)_\infty(q^3,q^6,q^7;q^{12})_\infty}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These identities are analytic forms of partition identities conjectured by Kanade and Russell. The paper proves many of them, including the identity for $H_{11}(1)$, so this combined historical conjecture is partially resolved; the supplied text does not establish that every displayed identity is proved.

344314.title: Conjectural combinatorial formula for the parabolic H-triangle
344314.statement:
For positive integers $m,n,t$, let $\operatorname{\bf NN}_{n,t}^{(m)}$ be the set of geometric multi-chains of $t$-filters. For $\mathcal V\in\operatorname{\bf NN}_{n,t}^{(m)}$, let $\operatorname{FL}(\mathcal V)$ denote its set of colored floors, let $S_{n,t}=\{(t,t+1),(t+1,t+2),\ldots,(n-1,n)\}$, and define

$$
\tilde H_{n,t}^{(m)}(x,y)=\sum_{\mathcal V\in\operatorname{\bf NN}_{n,t}^{(m)}}x^{|\operatorname{FL}(\mathcal V)|}y^{|\operatorname{FL}(\mathcal V)\cap S_{n,t}|}.
$$

**Combinatorial $H$-triangle conjecture.** For positive integers $m,n,t$,

$$
\tilde H_{n,t}^{(m)}(x,y)=H_{n,t}^{(m)}(x,y)
$$

with

$$
\tilde H_{n,t}^{(m)}(x,y)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-t}\sum_{h=0}^{n-t-k}\left(\binom{mn-t+1}{k}\binom{t+k+h-2}{h}-m\binom{mn-t}{k-1}\binom{t+k+h-1}{h}\right)x^{n-t-k}y^{n-t-k-h}.
$$

This asserts that the generating polynomial obtained from geometric multi-chains of $t$-filters equals the previously defined parabolic $H$-triangle. The supplied text does not state whether the identity has been proved or disproved.

350183.title: Baril and Kirgizov's continued-fraction conjecture for descents of type 2
350183.statement:
Let $cmathfrak{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements, and let $\operatorname{des}_2$ and $\operatorname{cyc}$ denote the descent-of-type-$2$ and cycle statistics. Let $y$, $lambda$, and $z$ be formal variables, and define $gamma_n=\lambda+2n$ and $lambda_n=(\lambda+n-1)(y+n-1)$.

**Baril and Kirgizov's continued-fraction conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{n\geq 0}\sum_{\sigma\in \mathfrak{S}_n} y^{\operatorname{des}_2\sigma} \lambda^{\operatorname{cyc}\sigma} \,z^n=\frac{1}{1-\lambda z-\cfrac{\lambda yz^2}{1-(\lambda+2)\, z- \cfrac{(\lambda+1)(y+1) z^2}{\cdots}}}
$$

with $gamma_n=\lambda+2n$ and $lambda_n=(\lambda+n-1)(y+n-1)$.

The source says this reformulates the first equidistribution conjecture using a theorem and a continued-fraction expression. The supplied text does not establish the displayed identity.

352082.title: Vlasev–Yeats conjecture on free variables in quadratic spanning forest identities
352082.statement: Let $m$ be the number of marked vertices in a graph. A quadratic spanning forest identity of the indicated type has coefficients as free variables, where the left-hand side consists of a spanning tree and a spanning forest with each marked vertex in a different tree, and the right-hand side consists of pairs of spanning forests partitioning the marked vertices between two and between $m-1$ trees. **Vlasev–Yeats conjecture.** The formulae for quadratic spanning forest identities of this type on $m$ marked vertices have $m(m-2)$ free variables. This conjecture generalizes the known 4-vertex identity, which has eight free variables; the paper subsequently gives a formal vector-space formulation and verifies the count in the cases discussed, while the general assertion is presented as a conjecture.

353418.title: Contraction conjecture for shortest homology basis loops in planar metric graphs
353418.statement: Let $X$ be a **planar metric graph**, meaning a geodesic space homeomorphic to a finite $1$-dimensional simplicial complex that admits a planar embedding. Let $G$ be a coefficient group, and let $\alpha\subset X$ be a simple closed loop such that its homology class $[\alpha]$ is a member of a shortest homology basis of $H_1(X;G)$. A **contraction** $X\to\alpha$ is a homotopy through maps from $X$ to itself from the identity map to a retraction onto $\alpha$. **Planar metric graph contraction conjecture.** There exists a contraction $X\to\alpha$. The conjecture asks whether planarity makes the condition that $[\alpha]$ belong to a shortest homology basis sufficient for contracting the entire metric graph onto $\alpha$; the preceding nonplanar examples show that the analogous assertion fails without planarity.

354386.title: The one-ended decidable-word-problem characterization of strongly aperiodic SFT groups
354386.statement:
Let $G$) be a finitely generated group. A group is **1-ended** if it has one end in the sense of ends of groups, and it has **decidable word problem** if there is an algorithm deciding whether a word over a finite generating set represents the identity in $G$. A **strongly aperiodic SFT** is a subshift of finite type over $G$ in which every configuration has trivial stabilizer.

**Strongly aperiodic SFT conjecture.** A finitely generated group admits a strongly aperiodic SFT if and only if it is 1-ended and has decidable word problem.

The conjecture seeks to characterize groups admitting strongly aperiodic finite-type symbolic dynamics. The cited results give the necessity of one-endedness and, under the stated hypotheses, decidability of the word problem, while many classes of one-ended groups with decidable word problem are known to admit such SFTs; the general equivalence remains open.

354873.title: Iterated W-algebra isomorphism conjecture for ordered partitions

360692.title: Perkins–Perarnau's coloring extremal conjecture for triangle-free and square-free cubic graphs
360692.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph, let $K_q$ be the complete graph on $q$ vertices, and let $\hom(G,K_q)$ denote the number of graph homomorphisms from $G$ to $K_q$. **Perkins–Perarnau's coloring extremal conjecture.** (a) Provided that $q\geq 4$, among $3$-regular triangle-free graphs $G$, the quantity

$$
\hom(G,K_q)^{1/|V(G)|}
$$

is minimized when $G$ is the Petersen graph. (b) Among $3$-regular graphs $G$ without cycles of length $4$, the quantity

$$
\hom(G,K_q)^{1/|V(G)|}
$$

is maximized when $G$ is the Heawood graph. These assertions propose the extremal cubic graphs for normalized proper $q$-coloring counts under the stated girth restrictions. The first assertion requires $q\geq 4$ because the source gives a counterexample at $q=3$; the status of the two assertions is otherwise left open in the source.

360978.title: Bressoud's partition identity conjecture for even moduli
360978.statement:
Let $A_j(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda;\eta,k,r;n)$ count partitions of $n$ into parts congruent to $0,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda\pmod{\eta}$ satisfying Bressoud's stated congruence and multiplicity conditions, and let $B_j(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda;\eta,k,r;n)$ count partitions of $n$ satisfying the corresponding difference, multiplicity, initial-condition, and parity conditions. For $j=0$ or $1$, $(2k+j)/2>r\geq\lambda\geq0$, and $n\geq0$, these two partition functions are equal:

**Bressoud's conjecture.**

$$
A_j(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda;\eta,k,r;n)=B_j(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda;\eta,k,r;n).
$$

This conjecture proposes an overpartition-free partition identity equating a congruence-side enumeration with a difference-condition enumeration for the indicated even-modulus parameters. Its resolution is not established by the supplied source context.

362858.title: Antidiagonal-permutation dominant-coefficient conjecture
362858.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, define the reversal permutation

$$
\pi_n \coloneqq \prod_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor n/2\right\rfloor}(i,n-i+1)\in\mathfrak{S}_n.
$$

Let $r_n^{\pi_n}$ be the corresponding element of $\mathfrak{U}_{\mathsf{DY}}^1$, and let $p_{n,m}$ denote the coefficient of $r_{n+m}^{\pi_{n+m}}$ in the product $r_n^{\mathsf{id}}\circ r_m^{\pi_m}$. **Antidiagonal-permutation dominant-coefficient conjecture.** The identity

$$
r_1^{\mathsf{id}}\circ r_n^{\pi_n}=-n\,r_{n+1}^{\pi_{n+1}}+r_n^{\pi_n}\star r_1^{\mathsf{id}}+\sum_{i=1}^n r_{n+1}^{\pi_{n+1}\circ(i,i+1)}
$$

holds in $\mathfrak{U}_{\mathsf{DY}}^1$; moreover, $p_{n,m}$ is the dominant coefficient of $r_1^{\mathsf{id}}\circ r_n^{\pi_n}$, and

$$
p_{n,m}=(-1)^n\bigl(\lvert p_{n-1,m}\rvert+\lvert p_{n,m-1}\rvert\bigr)
$$

with $p_{1,1}=-1$, $p_{1,m}=-m$, and $p_{n,1}=0$ for $n>1$. This conjecture proposes a distinguished family of leading coefficients and a recurrence for them; the supplied text gives no evidence of resolution.

369935.title: Simplicial-tree characterisation from an intermediate face number
369935.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$, let $p$ be the number of vertices, and let $K$ be a pure $n$-simplicial complex. For some $0\leq m\leq n-1$, an $(m,n)$-simplicial cycle sequence is the cycle-sequence notion used in the paper, and $\alpha_k(K)$ denotes the number of $k$-simplices of $K$. **The simplicial-tree conjecture.** The complex $K$ is a simplicial tree if and only if it satisfies all three conditions: it has no $(m,n)$-simplicial cycle sequences for some $0\leq m\leq n-1$; for some $1\leq k\leq n-1$, 

$$
\alpha_k(K)=(p-n)\binom{n}{k}+\binom{n}{k+1};
$$

and

$$
\alpha_n(K)=p-n.
$$

The conjecture asks whether the top-dimensional face-count condition in the preceding theorem can be replaced by knowledge of an intermediate face number. The authors state that they have neither a proof nor a counterexample.
